meta: AI has no window and no phone. So how does it know if it will rain tomorrow? The secret: AI doesn't press buttons itself. It just writes a "request slip", called a tool call, and the app does the rest.
prompt: What's the price of gold this morning?

muc.title: AI has no window
muc.text: You ask AI whether it will rain in Da Lat tomorrow, and it answers right away, with the temperature too. But AI has no window and no phone. So where did that come from?

muc.title: AI can only write
muc.text: The secret: AI doesn't press any buttons itself. It can only write text. So when it needs outside information, it writes a request slip, called a tool call.

muc.title: The slip makes a round trip
muc.text: The slip says: use the weather tool, place Da Lat, tomorrow. The app reads the slip, asks a weather service, then hands the result back to AI.

muc.title: Only then does it answer
muc.text: With the result in hand, AI writes its answer to you. That whole loop is called tool calling: AI calling a tool.

muc.title: A tool board on the wall
muc.text: Each tool is one line of description: its name, what it does, what information it needs. AI reads that list to know when to use which one. Web search, checking a calendar, doing math: they all work this way.

muc.title: The app holds the power
muc.text: Because AI only writes slips, the power to act stays with the app. If a slip asks to send email or pay money, a good app stops and asks you first.

muc.title: Catch the slip in action
muc.text: Ask AI about something happening today, like this morning's gold price. Watch for the small "searching" text. That's the moment it sends a request slip.

muc.title: A hundred kinds of slips
muc.text: But every app uses its own kind of slip. To connect AI to a hundred tools, do you have to build it a hundred times? Part two: a shared port called MCP.
